title: $\eta$ is compatible with composition
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a condensed ring, and let $f\colon X\to Y$ and $g\colon Y\to Z$ be morphisms of schemes.

For every scheme $T$, write $\pi_T\colon T\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ for its structure morphism. Let $p^*$ be the inverse-image functor from the point used in [def-sfb-upper-star-from-point], put $F=p^*\Lambda$, and write $\Lambda_T=\pi_T^*F$ for the coefficient object of [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients].

Use the following explicit source construction of the pullback composition comparisons in [def-sfb-pullback-from-point-comp-iso], [def-sfb-alpha] and [def-sfb-eta]. For any composable scheme morphisms $a\colon A\to B$, $b\colon B\to C$, let $c_{a,b}\colon b_*a_*\xrightarrow{\sim}(b\circ a)_*$ be [def-sfb-finite-lower-star-comp]. Under the adjunctions of [def-sfb-finite-upper-lower-star-adjunction], including the composite adjunction of [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction], define
$$
m_{a,b}\colon a^*b^*\xrightarrow{\sim}(b\circ a)^*
$$
to be the unique comparison corresponding to $c_{a,b}^{-1}$ by [lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation]: use $L_1=a^*b^*$, $R_1=b_*a_*$, $L_2=(b\circ a)^*$, $R_2=(b\circ a)_*$ and $\delta=c_{a,b}^{-1}$ there. The forward pullback composition comparison is $m_{a,b}^{-1}$. Equivalently, by the conjugation bijection of [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate], the conjugate of $m_{a,b}$ is $c_{a,b}^{-1}$. Thus for $h\colon A\to B$, $\alpha_h$ is $(m_{h,\pi_B})_{p^*\Lambda}$ after the canonical equality $\pi_B\circ h=\pi_A$, and $\eta_h$ is its adjunct as in [def-sfb-eta]. This fixes the comparison by construction, rather than imposing an additional condition on $a,b$ or $\Lambda$.

Then
$$
\eta_{g\circ f}=(c_{f,g})_{\Lambda_X}\circ g_*(\eta_f)\circ\eta_g\colon
\Lambda_Z\longrightarrow(g\circ f)_*\Lambda_X.
$$

proof.text: Work in sheaves of abelian groups, with ordinary (not derived) functors. Write $k_T=\pi_T:T\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ and $F=p^*\Lambda$. By [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients] and [def-sfb-upper-star-from-point], $\Lambda_T=k_T^*F$. Write $u_h$ for the unit of $h^*\dashv h_*$ from [def-sfb-finite-upper-lower-star-adjunction]. For $h:A\to B$, the equality $k_B\circ h=k_A$ and [def-sfb-pullback-from-point-comp-iso, def-sfb-alpha] identify $\alpha_h:h^*k_B^*F\to k_A^*F$ with the inverse pullback composition comparison evaluated at $F$. By [def-sfb-eta], $\eta_h=h_*(\alpha_h)\circ u_{h,k_B^*F}$. Put $v_T=u_{k_T,F}:F\to k_{T*}\Lambda_T$.

source.place: paragraph 1: identify the coefficient maps and fix units

proof.text:
For $h\colon A\to B$, let $c_{h,k_B}\colon k_{B*}h_*\xrightarrow{\sim}k_{A*}$ be [def-sfb-finite-lower-star-comp], using $k_B\circ h=k_A$. Apply the actual comparison construction in the statement: $m_{h,k_B}$ is the unique natural isomorphism supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation] with $L_1=h^*k_B^*$, $R_1=k_{B*}h_*$, $L_2=k_A^*$, $R_2=k_{A*}$ and $\delta=c_{h,k_B}^{-1}$. By the bijection of [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate] this is precisely the inverse conjugate of $c_{h,k_B}^{-1}$; in particular it is the inverse of the forward pullback comparison, not that forward comparison. By [def-sfb-pullback-from-point-comp-iso, def-sfb-alpha] and the explicit source normalization in the statement, $(m_{h,k_B})_F=\alpha_h$. By [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction] the unit for $L_1\dashv R_1$ at $F$ is $k_{B*}(u_{h,k_B^*F})\circ v_B$. The cited unit equation therefore reads
$$
k_{B*}h_*(\alpha_h)\circ k_{B*}(u_{h,k_B^*F})\circ v_B
=(c_{h,k_B}^{-1})_{\Lambda_A}\circ v_A.
$$
Functoriality and the defining formula for $\eta_h$ in step 1 give
$$
k_{B*}(\eta_h)\circ v_B=(c_{h,k_B}^{-1})_{\Lambda_A}\circ v_A.\tag{1}
$$
This applies to $h=f,g,g\circ f$. It uses the explicit construction and the unit equation of the cited leaf; it takes no mate identity from the incorrectly oriented imported comparison definition.

proof.text:
For every sheaf $H$ on $X_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}}$, the comparisons of [def-sfb-finite-lower-star-comp] satisfy
$$ (c_{g\circ f,k_Z})_H\circ k_{Z*}((c_{f,g})_H)
=(c_{f,k_Y})_H\circ(c_{g,k_Z})_{f_*H}.\tag{2}$$
Indeed [def-sfb-finite-lower-star] computes each pushforward by restriction along base change. Evaluate on $V\in(\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z)_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}}$. Both composites in (2) restrict $H$ along the same canonical isomorphism between $((V\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}Z)\times_ZY)\times_YX$ and $V\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}X$. The two maps have the same projections to $V$ and $X$, so they agree by the defining universal property of the fibre product; their inverses agree as well. Restriction is functorial, hence the resulting maps on sections agree for every $V$, proving (2). At $H=\Lambda_X$, compose (2) with the inverse comparisons to obtain
$$ k_{Z*}((c_{f,g})_{\Lambda_X})\circ(c_{g,k_Z}^{-1})_{f_*\Lambda_X}\circ(c_{f,k_Y}^{-1})_{\Lambda_X}
=(c_{g\circ f,k_Z}^{-1})_{\Lambda_X}.\tag{3}$$

source.place: paragraph 4: associativity on sections, including its inverse form

proof.text:
Set $t=(c_{f,g})_{\Lambda_X}\circ g_*(\eta_f)\circ\eta_g$. Its transpose under $k_Z^*\dashv k_{Z*}$ is $k_{Z*}(t)\circ v_Z$, by the Hom bijection of [def-sfb-finite-upper-lower-star-adjunction]. Expand functoriality, then apply (1) for $g$:
$$k_{Z*}(t)\circ v_Z=k_{Z*}((c_{f,g})_{\Lambda_X})\circ k_{Z*}g_*(\eta_f)\circ(c_{g,k_Z}^{-1})_{\Lambda_Y}\circ v_Y.$$
Naturality of the isomorphism $c_{g,k_Z}^{-1}$ from [def-sfb-finite-lower-star-comp] at the morphism $\eta_f:\Lambda_Y\to f_*\Lambda_X$ gives
$$k_{Z*}g_*(\eta_f)\circ(c_{g,k_Z}^{-1})_{\Lambda_Y}=(c_{g,k_Z}^{-1})_{f_*\Lambda_X}\circ k_{Y*}(\eta_f).$$
Substitute this, then (1) for $f$, then (3). The result is
$$k_{Z*}(t)\circ v_Z=(c_{g\circ f,k_Z}^{-1})_{\Lambda_X}\circ v_X.$$
By (1) for $g\circ f$, this is also $k_{Z*}(\eta_{g\circ f})\circ v_Z$.

source.place: paragraph 3: explicitly expand the two transposes and the naturality square

proof.text: The Hom correspondence for $k_Z^*\dashv k_{Z*}$ in [def-sfb-finite-upper-lower-star-adjunction] is a bijection, so equality of the transposes in step 4 implies $t=\eta_{g\circ f}$. This is precisely the claimed identity with the composition comparison evaluated at $\Lambda_X$.

lemma condensedPushforwardHom_comp {Z : Scheme.{u}} (g : Y ⟶ Z) :
    condensedPushforwardHom Λ (f ≫ g) =
      condensedPushforwardHom Λ g ≫ (g)_*[Ab.{u + 1}].map (condensedPushforwardHom Λ f) ≫
        (ProEtale.lowerStarComp Ab.{u + 1} f g).hom.app (condensedRingObj Λ X)
lean.note: Exact existing theorem in the published pro-etale module-object framework, read through scompile.py --source. The section binds Λ : Sheaf (coherentTopology Profinite.{u}) Ab.{u + 1}, arbitrary X Y : Scheme.{u}, and f : X ⟶ Y; the theorem binds arbitrary Z and g. The section's MonObj instance is explicitly omitted since the equality is on underlying abelian sheaves, so it applies in particular to every condensed ring without a commutativity condition. condensedPushforwardHom is the recorded eta, and lowerStarComp.hom at condensedRingObj Λ X is the recorded c_{f,g} at Λ_X. The construction also agrees with the node's explicit normalization: upperStarComp is the inverse of (conjugateIsoEquiv adjCompositeScheme adjComposite).symm (lowerStarComp.symm); hence its inverse is exactly m_{a,b} with conjugate c_{a,b}^{-1}. upperStarFromPointComp uses that inverse followed by comp_toSpecZ, and condensedPullbackHom is its component at Λ. The branch label denotes the published WeilConjectures source root, resolved by the side overlay rather than the older local slopmaster2 checkout. No new module or construction is introduced.
